Application Materials.content:
Required supporting documents for the MSc in Business Analytics application:
| Document | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Personal statement | This should be approximately 500 words in length. |
| Official transcript | If required, please provide a certified English translation. |
| Degree certificate | If required, please provide a certified English translation. This is not required for current students. |
| English language qualification | See Entry Requirements for accepted certificates. |
Please note that the Business School reserves the right to verify documents submitted within your application.
A reference is not required as part of your application; however, if you wish to submit a reference in support of your application, you are welcome to. **We reserve the right to request a reference during the application review process. If requested, you will need to submit a suitable reference before we can deliver a result for your application.**
[Admissions documents guidance](https://www.business-school.ed.ac.uk/msc/admissions-documents)
Personal statement guidance: the School will be looking for evidence that you have thought carefully about what you can bring to the programme and what impact you feel it will have on your future career. Address the following issues:
- What skills, qualities and experiences have prepared you to undertake this programme?
- What value do you think you can add to the learning community as part of an internationally diverse group?
- What impact do you hope to make in your future career, and how will this programme contribute to your aspirations?
Your personal statement should be around 500 words in length. The information you give must be true. Copying information from elsewhere or asking someone else to write your statement, including the use of AI apps such as Chat GPT, could be considered fraud.
For further information regarding references during the application process, visit the University's [references page](https://www.ed.ac.uk/studying/postgraduate/applying/your-application/references).

| Round | Application Deadline | Decisions By |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **15 October 2025** | 4 December 2025 |
| 2 | **10 December 2025** | 19 February 2026 |
| 3 | **11 February 2026** | 23 April 2026 |
| 4 | **22 April 2026** | 4 June 2026 |
| 5 | **10 June 2026** | 23 July 2026 |
If your programme has an application fee, you must pay this within 5 working days of the application deadline in order for your submission to be considered in that round. In each cycle you will be able to submit an application until the programme closes for admissions. If the programme is not full by the final application deadline, applications submitted after that date will continue to be considered. If you require a visa, submit your application by the **final round 5 application deadline**.

Academic Requirements.content:
Entrance to the **MSc in Business Analytics** is strongly competitive; applicants can increase their chances by exceeding the minimum programme requirements.
- You will need a **UK first-class or 2:1 honours degree** in a related subject, or an **equivalent overseas qualification**.
- An undergraduate degree in any disciplinary area related to **management science, operational research, statistics, econometrics, mathematics, physics, computer science, engineering, or business and management** which incorporates a distinct quantitative element is required.
- Candidates with a first-class or 2:1 honours degree in an unrelated subject area but who have relevant work experience will be considered on an individual basis.
- Candidates' background should ideally include courses and/or experience in topics such as **linear algebra, calculus, probability, statistics, and computer programming**.
- Relevant work experience is not required but may increase your chances of acceptance.
- Relevant professional qualifications will be considered.
- Preference will be given to those with grades above the minimum requirements due to strong competition for places on this programme.
- Final year undergraduate students are welcome to apply, so long as their studies will be completed prior to the MSc programme commencement date.
- If your degree is not of the required standard and you do not have highly relevant work or other experience, the application will normally be rejected.
- Meeting the degree requirement does not ensure acceptance; a higher standard may be needed for admission or funding.
- A conditional offer can be made if you are waiting for a final degree result.
International qualification examples for the minimum academic requirement include:
- Canada: **B+; 3.25+ (4 point scale); 7+ (9 point scale)**
- China: **85%+; Band A from the [Priority list of Chinese universities](https://www.ed.ac.uk/sites/default/files/atoms/files/priority_list_of_chinese_universities.pdf)**
- Germany: **2.2+ (reverse 5 point scale); Sehr Gut/Gut**
- India: **1st Class degree (60%+); 3.2 on a 4 point scale; 8.0 on a 10 point scale**
- Nigeria: **2:1**
- South Africa: **2:1/1st**
- USA: **GPA 3.25+ (4 point scale)**
For applicants from China: this degree programme is **Band A**, requiring a **minimum of 85% awarded by a Chinese university on the Priority List**. General Edinburgh China guidance states that postgraduate taught applicants should have a first degree from a university on the Priority List of Chinese universities or a recognised university, with minimum grades between **80-85%**; for **Band A**, the requirement is **a minimum of 85% awarded by a university on the Priority List**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Regardless of nationality or country of residence, applicants must demonstrate a level of English language competency which will enable them to succeed in their studies.
Accepted English language qualifications at the specified grades:
- [IELTS Academic](https://www.ielts.org/): **total 7.0 with at least 6.0 in each component**. IELTS One Skill Retake is not accepted.
- [TOEFL iBT](http://www.ets.org/toefl) (including Home Edition) before 21 January 2026: **total 100 with at least 20 in each component**. TOEFL MyBest Score is not accepted.
- [TOEFL iBT](http://www.ets.org/toefl) (including Home Edition) from 21 January 2026: **total 5.0 with at least 4.0 in each component**. TOEFL MyBest Score is not accepted.
- [C1 Advanced](https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/advanced/) (formerly CAE) / [C2 Proficiency](http://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/proficiency/) (formerly CPE): **total 185 with at least 169 in each component**.
- [Trinity ISE](https://www.trinitycollege.com/site/?id=3287): **ISE III with passes in all four components**.
- [Oxford ELLT](https://oxfordellt.com/) (Global and Digital): **8 overall with at least 6 in each component**.
Unless the applicant is a national of a majority English speaking country, the English language qualification must be no more than **three and a half years old** from the start of the month in which the programme begins. IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, Trinity ISE, or Oxford ELLT tests must be no more than **two years old** on the first of the month in which the programme begins, regardless of nationality.
The University also accepts an undergraduate or postgraduate degree taught and assessed in a majority English speaking country, as defined by UK Visas and Immigration: [UKVI list of majority English speaking countries](https://www.gov.uk/tier-4-general-visa/knowledge-of-english). It also accepts a degree taught and assessed in English from a university on the approved list: [Approved universities in non-majority English speaking countries](https://www.ed.ac.uk/studying/postgraduate/applying/your-application/entry-requirements/english-requirements/approved-universities). If the applicant is not a national of a majority English speaking country, the degree must be no more than **five years old** at the start of the month in which the programme begins.
Applicants may include an existing English language certificate with the application. If they have not yet taken a test, the application will still be processed and results can be uploaded later. A conditional offer may be given if the applicant does not yet meet the minimum English requirement, but evidence of meeting the minimum English requirement must be provided before an unconditional offer can be issued.
Optional pre-sessional English courses are available through English Language Education. General English for Academic Purposes is intended for international students who need to improve their English before starting a programme; the end-of-course assessment can be used to meet the English requirements of their Masters programme beginning in September. [English for Academic Purposes summer courses](https://www.ed.ac.uk/english-language-teaching/pre-sessional-english/summer-eap-courses)

Program Overview.content:
Our MSc Business Analytics programme equips students with the computational and analytical skills demanded by employers. In an increasingly data-driven age, organisations are looking for innovative ways to use business intelligence data to gain a competitive edge. Through a curriculum that combines theoretical knowledge with practical application, this master's degree will empower you with the ability to transform raw data into impactful insights.
- **Programme structure:** The MSc Business Analytics programme offers the opportunity to develop advanced knowledge in specific areas of analytics before specialising through a choice of option courses. [View programme structure](https://www.business-school.ed.ac.uk/msc/business-analytics/overview/programme-structure)
- **Learning outcomes:** The programme enables students to recognise, understand, and apply the language, theory, and models of business analytics and improve problem-solving abilities. [View the learning outcomes](https://www.business-school.ed.ac.uk/msc/business-analytics/overview/learning-outcomes)
- **Industry opportunities:** Students can participate in industry treks, group consultancy, client sourced dissertations, and benefit from speaking to a variety of industry professionals. [Engagement with industry](https://www.business-school.ed.ac.uk/msc/business-analytics/overview/industry-opportunities)

Cost of Attendance.content:
For 2026-2027, the University estimates that it will cost an average of **£18,504 each year (£1,542 each month)** to live in Edinburgh as a postgraduate. This amount does not include study costs like tuition fees.
| Living cost item | Per month | Per 52-week year |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Accommodation and utilities** | £978 | £11,736 |
| **Food and other shopping** | £248 | £2,976 |
| **Mobile phone contract** | £12 | £144 |
| **Socialising, leisure and wellbeing** | £246 | £2,952 |
| **Local bus travel (age 22+)** | £58 | £696 |
| Estimated total living costs | **£1,542** | **£18,504** |
Accommodation and utilities are estimated at **£752 to £1,249 per month**. Accommodation options for postgraduate students include:
| Cost item | University | Private | Private student |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Rent for accommodation** | £918 per month (ranging from £388 to £1,596) | £688 per month | £1,227 per month (ranging from £659 to £1,781) |
| **Utilities (gas and electric)** | Included in rent | £55 per month | Included in rent |
| **WiFi** | Included in rent | £9 per month | Included in rent |
| **Laundry services** | £13 per month | Washing machines normally in flats | £22 per month |
| Estimated total | **£931 per month** | **£752 per month** | **£1,249 per month** |
Food and other shopping is estimated at **£248 per month**. Mobile phone contract is estimated at **£12 per month**. Socialising, leisure and wellbeing is estimated at **£246 per month**. Local bus travel is estimated at **£58 per month**, or **£660 for an annual advance purchase pass**; students under 22 can get free bus travel.
Students will not need to pay for healthcare or prescriptions, as these are free for students in Scotland. However, international students need to pay a health surcharge to access the National Health Service (NHS) as part of their visa application.

Multiple Applications.content: We recommend that you submit only one or two applications in order to have the best possible chance of receiving a positive outcome. We understand that you may find it difficult to choose between one or two related degree programmes, and we are prepared to consider more than one application in those circumstances. However, **we cannot consider more than five applications from the same applicant**, and this number may be lower in high demand areas.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Each year we have limited capacity for deferred offers. All deferral requests will be considered on an individual basis.
- The deadline for submitting a deferral request is **31 August**.
- If your deferral request is unsuccessful, you are encouraged to take up your place for entry this year, or to withdraw and submit a new application for entry next year when applications open. Because competition for places varies each year, there is no guarantee that a new application will be successful.
- If you defer your place you may need to take a new English test if your current English language qualification expires before the revised start date. The new SELT will be required by **31 October** of your original entry year.
- The deposit must be paid before a deferral is agreed. This should be done within **28 days** of receiving the original offer. The deposit is non-refundable.
- We defer unconditional offers only. It is possible to defer an offer only once.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
- Final year undergraduate students are welcome to apply, so long as your studies will be **completed prior to the MSc programme commencement date**.
- A conditional offer can be made if you are waiting for a **final degree result** or a **language test result**.
- A conditional offer may be given if you do not yet meet the minimum English requirement, but you must provide evidence that you have reached the **minimum English requirement** before an unconditional offer can be provided.
- If you require a visa, you must have achieved your English qualification and have met any other conditions to qualify for an unconditional offer, which is a requirement for the CAS. The University will commence issuing CAS from **June onwards**.
- Optional pre-sessional English courses are available. General English for Academic Purposes is intended for international students who need to improve their English language level before commencing study; at the end of the course, students undertake an assessment which can be used to meet the English requirements of their Masters programme beginning in September.
